source.title: Lesson 0002: Safe Binary File I/O & ROM Loading into Memory at 0x200

cards.question: Why must binary files be opened with mode "rb" instead of "r" in C?
cards.answer: Opening in text mode ("r") can perform platform-specific newline translations, silently corrupting raw binary executable bytecode.

cards.question: What is the maximum allowable ROM size when loading a program into CHIP-8 RAM?
cards.answer: 3,584 bytes (4,096 bytes total RAM minus 512 bytes reserved for fontset and interpreter below 0x200).

cards.question: Why must rewind(file) or fseek(file, 0, SEEK_SET) be called before reading after checking file size with fseek/ftell?
cards.answer: Seeking to the end moves the file position indicator to EOF; without rewinding back to the beginning, fread would read 0 bytes.

cards.question: What does fopen return upon failure to open a file in C?
cards.answer: fopen returns NULL when opening a file fails (such as when the file is missing or permissions are denied).

cards.question: Where is the built-in 80-byte hexadecimal font set stored in CHIP-8 memory?
cards.answer: The font set is stored in the reserved memory region from 0x000 to 0x050.
